nodes.name: Hörmander multipliers are Calderón-Zygmund operators
nodes.statement: As for example, well-known Calder\'on-Zygmund operators are the Fourier multipliers associated to a symbol $m$ satisfying H\"ormander's condition $$ | \partial^\alpha m(\xi)| \lesssim |\xi|^{-|\alpha|}=d(\xi,0)^{-|\alpha|},$$ which encodes regularity assumption of the symbol relatively to the frequency $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Fourier multipliers whose symbol satisfies Hörmander's condition are classical Calderón-Zygmund operators.
assumptions: a symbol $m$ satisfying H\"ormander's condition $$ | \partial^\alpha m(\xi)| \lesssim |\xi|^{-|\alpha|}=d(\xi,0)^{-|\alpha|},$$
conclusions: well-known Calder\'on-Zygmund operators are the Fourier multipliers

nodes.name: Multi-frequency Hörmander condition
nodes.statement: More precisely, let $\Theta:=(\xi_1,...,\xi_N)$ be a collection of frequencies and consider a symbol $m$ verifying for all multi-indices $\alpha$ $$ | \partial^\alpha m(\xi)| \lesssim d(\xi,\Theta)^{-|\alpha|},$$ with $d(\xi,\Theta):= \min_{1\leq i \leq N} |\xi-\xi_i|$. Such symbols give rise to Fourier multipliers, which should be the prototype of what we want to call {\it multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators}.
nodes.statement_short: Symbols with $|\partial^\alpha m(\xi)|\lesssim d(\xi,\Theta)^{-|\alpha|}$, $d$ the distance to the frequency set, prototypes of multi-frequency CZ operators.

nodes.name: Multi-frequency Calderón-Zygmund operator
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta:=(\xi_1,...,\xi_N)$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies of ${\mathbb R}^n$. An $L^2$-bounded linear operator $T$ is said to be a Calder\'on-Zygmund operator relatively to $\Theta$ if there exist operators $(T_j)_{j=1,...,N}$ and kernels $(K_j)_{j=1,...,N}$ verifying \begin{itemize} \item Decomposition: $T=\sum_{j=1}^N T_j$; \item Integral representation of $T_j$: for every function $f\in L^2$ compactly supported and $x\in \textrm{supp}(f)^{c}$, $$ T_j(f)(x) = \int K_j(x,y) f(y);$$ \item Regularity of the modulated kernels: for every $x\neq y$ $$ \sum_{j=1}^N \left|\nabla_{(x,y)}\ e^{i\xi_j\cdot(x-y)} K_j(x,y)\right| \lesssim |x-y|^{-n-1}.$$ \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: An $L^2$-bounded $T=\sum_j T_j$ with kernels $K_j$ whose modulations $e^{i\xi_j\cdot(x-y)}K_j$ jointly satisfy a CZ gradient bound.

nodes.name: Hölder regularity suffices
nodes.statement: As usual, we can weaken the regularity assumption and just require an $\epsilon$-H\"older regularity on the modulated kernels.

nodes.name: Orthogonal decompositions give constant of order N
nodes.statement: If the decomposition is assumed to be orthogonal (which means that for $i\neq j$, $T_iT_j^*=0$) then it follows that each operator $T_j$ is a modulated Calder\'on-Zygmund operator. Such a multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator can also be pointwisely bounded by a sum of $N$ modulated (classical) Calder\'on-Zygmund operators and have the same boundedness properties with an implicit constant of order $N$. The aim is to study how this order can be improved using sharp estimates.
nodes.statement_short: With orthogonal decomposition each $T_j$ is a modulated CZ operator, giving bounds with constant $O(N)$; the aim is to improve this.

nodes.name: Unweighted bounds for multi-frequency Calderón-Zygmund operators
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies and $T$ an associated multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator. Then \begin{itemize} \item for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $T$ is bounded on $L^p$ with $$ \|T\|_{L^p \to L^p} \lesssim N^{\left|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}\right|}.$$ \item for $p=1$, $T$ is of weak-type $(1,1)$ with $$ \|T\|_{L^1 \to L^{1,\infty}} \lesssim N^{\frac{1}{2}}.$$ \end{itemize}
assumptions: Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies and $T$ an associated multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator.
conclusions: for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $T$ is bounded on $L^p$ with $$ \|T\|_{L^p \to L^p} \lesssim N^{\left|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}\right|}.$$
for $p=1$, $T$ is of weak-type $(1,1)$ with $$ \|T\|_{L^1 \to L^{1,\infty}} \lesssim N^{\frac{1}{2}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Multi-frequency CZ operators are $L^p$-bounded with norm $\lesssim N^{|1/p-1/2|}$ and weak $(1,1)$ with norm $\lesssim N^{1/2}$.
nodes.label: thm:boundedness

nodes.name: Weighted boundedness of Calderón-Zygmund operators
nodes.statement: Concerning weighted estimates, it is well-known that linear Calder\'on-Zygmund operators are bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ for $p\in(1,\infty)$ and every weight $\omega$ belonging to the Muckenhoupt's class ${\mathbb A}_p$ (see Definitions \ref{def:1} and \ref{def:2} for more details about Muckenhoupt's class ${\mathbb A}_p$ and Reverse H\"older class $RH_s$).
assumptions: $p\in(1,\infty)$ and every weight $\omega$ belonging to the Muckenhoupt's class ${\mathbb A}_p$
conclusions: linear Calder\'on-Zygmund operators are bounded on $L^p(\omega)$

nodes.name: Johnson-Neugebauer change of variables for weights
nodes.statement: From \cite{JN}, we know that for $r,s>1$, $$ {\mathbb A}_{r} \cap RH_s = \left\{\omega, \omega^{s} \in{\mathbb A}_{1+s(r-1)}\right\},$$ so these classes of weights are equivalent to a class of powers of Muckenhoupt's weights.
conclusions: $$ {\mathbb A}_{r} \cap RH_s = \left\{\omega, \omega^{s} \in{\mathbb A}_{1+s(r-1)}\right\},$$
nodes.statement_short: $A_r\cap RH_s$ consists of the weights whose $s$-th power lies in $A_{1+s(r-1)}$.

nodes.name: Weighted bounds for multi-frequency Calderón-Zygmund operators
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies. For $p\in (1,\infty)$, $s\in(1,p)$ and $t\in(1,\infty)$, then every multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator $T$ is bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ for every weight $\omega \in RH_{t'} \cap {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$ with $$ \|T\|_{L^p(\omega) \to L^p(\omega)} \lesssim N^{\gamma}$$ and $$ \gamma:=\frac{tp}{s\min\{2,s\}}+\left|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}\right|.$$ We emphasize that this result is only interesting when $\gamma<1$.
assumptions: Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies.
For $p\in (1,\infty)$, $s\in(1,p)$ and $t\in(1,\infty)$
conclusions: every multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator $T$ is bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ for every weight $\omega \in RH_{t'} \cap {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$ with $$ \|T\|_{L^p(\omega) \to L^p(\omega)} \lesssim N^{\gamma}$$
nodes.statement_short: For weights in $RH_{t'}\cap A_{p/s}$, multi-frequency CZ operators are bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ with norm $\lesssim N^\gamma$, $\gamma$ explicit.
nodes.label: thm:weight

nodes.name: Center and radius of a ball
nodes.statement: Given a ball $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ we denote its center by $c(Q)$ and its radius by $r_Q$.

nodes.name: Average of a function
nodes.statement: For a subset $E\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of finite and non-vanishing measure and $f$ a locally integrable function, the average of $f$ on $E$ is defined by $$ \aver{E} f dx := \frac{1}{|E|}\int_E f(x) dx.$$

nodes.name: Collection of all balls

nodes.name: Hardy-Littlewood maximal function
nodes.statement: We write ${\mathcal M}$ for the maximal Hardy-Littlewood function: $$ {\mathcal M} f(x)= \sup_{{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{Q\in{\mathcal Q}}{x\in Q}}} \aver{Q}|f|dx.$$

nodes.name: L^p maximal function
nodes.statement: For $p\in (1,\infty)$, we set ${\mathcal M}_p f(x)={\mathcal M}(|f|^p)(x)^{1/p}$.

nodes.name: Fourier transform notation
nodes.statement: The Fourier transform will be denoted by $\mathcal F$ as an operator and we make use of the other usual notation ${\mathcal F}(f)=\widehat{f}$ too.

nodes.name: Nikolskii-type inequality (Borwein-Erdélyi)
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta\subset {\mathbb R}^n$ be a finite collection of frequencies and $Q$ be a ball. For every function $\phi$ belonging to the subspace of $L^2(3Q)$, spanned by $(e^{i\xi\cdot})_{\xi\in \Theta}$, we have for $p\in[1,2]$ \begin{equation} \|\phi\|_{L^\infty(Q)} \lesssim (\sharp \Theta)^{\frac{1}{p}} \left(\aver{3Q} |\phi|^p dx \right)^{\frac{1}{p}}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries
assumptions: Let $\Theta\subset {\mathbb R}^n$ be a finite collection of frequencies and $Q$ be a ball.
For every function $\phi$ belonging to the subspace of $L^2(3Q)$, spanned by $(e^{i\xi\cdot})_{\xi\in \Theta}$
for $p\in[1,2]$
conclusions: \|\phi\|_{L^\infty(Q)} \lesssim (\sharp \Theta)^{\frac{1}{p}} \left(\aver{3Q} |\phi|^p dx \right)^{\frac{1}{p}}.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential sums with $N$ frequencies satisfy $\|\phi\|_{L^\infty(Q)}\lesssim N^{1/p}$ times their $L^p$ average on $3Q$, for $p\in[1,2]$.
nodes.label: lem

nodes.name: Nikolskii-type inequality (1)
nodes.statement: \|\phi\|_{L^\infty(Q)} \lesssim (\sharp \Theta)^{\frac{1}{p}} \left(\aver{3Q} |\phi|^p dx \right)^{\frac{1}{p}}.
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries
nodes.label: aze

nodes.name: Multi-dimensional extension of the lemma
nodes.statement: In \cite{BE}, this lemma is stated and proved in a one-dimensional setting. However, the proof only relies on the additive group structure of the ambient space by using translation operators. So the exact same proof can be extended to a multi-dimensional setting.
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries

nodes.name: Extension of the lemma for p ≥ 2
nodes.statement: The question of extending the previous lemma for $p\in(2,\infty)$ is still open in such a general situation. Of course, (\ref{aze}) is true for $p=\infty$ and so it would be reasonable to expect the result for intermediate exponents $p \in(2,\infty)$. Unfortunately, the well-known interpolation theory does not apply here. \\ However, in some specific situations, we may extend this lemma for $p\geq 2$. Indeed, if $p=2k$ is an even integer then applying (\ref{aze}) with $p=2$ and $\Theta^k:=\{\theta_{i_1}+...+\theta_{i_k},\ \theta_i\in \Theta\}$ to $\phi^k$ yields \begin{align*} \|\phi \|_{L^\infty(Q)} & \lesssim \|\phi^k \|_{L^\infty(Q)}^{\frac{1}{k}} \\ & \lesssim (\sharp \Theta^k )^{\frac{1}{2k}} \left(\aver{3Q} |\phi|^{2k} dx \right)^{\frac{1}{2k}} \\ & \simeq (\sharp \Theta^k )^{\frac{1}{p}} \left(\aver{3Q} |\phi|^{p} dx \right)^{\frac{1}{p}}. \end{align*} By this way, we see that an extension of (\ref{aze}) for $p\geq 2$ may be related to sharp combinatorial arguments, to estimate $\sharp \Theta^k$ (a trivial bound is $\sharp \Theta^k \leq (\sharp \Theta)^{k}$ which does not improve (\ref{aze})).
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: Extending Lemma 1.1 to $p>2$ is open; for even $p=2k$ it follows by applying the $p=2$ case to $\phi^k$, at the cost of $\sharp\Theta^k$.
nodes.label: rem:lem

nodes.name: Lemma 1.1 for p in (2, infinity)
nodes.statement: The question of extending the previous lemma for $p\in(2,\infty)$ is still open in such a general situation.
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: Does the Nikolskii-type inequality of Lemma 1.1 extend to $p\in(2,\infty)$ for general frequency sets?

nodes.name: Muckenhoupt class A_p
nodes.statement: A weight $\omega$ is a non-negative locally integrable function. We say that a weight $\omega\in {\mathbb A}_p$, $1<p<\infty$, if there exists a positive constant $C$ such that for every ball $Q$, $$\bigg(\aver{Q} \omega\,dx\bigg)\, \bigg(\aver{Q} \omega^{1-p'}\,dx\bigg)^{p-1}\le C. $$ For $p=1$, we say that $\omega\in {\mathbb A}_1$ if there is a positive constant $C$ such that for every ball $Q$, $$ \aver{Q} \omega \,dx \le C\, \omega (y), \qquad \mbox{for a.e. }y\in Q. $$ We write ${\mathbb A}_\infty=\cup_{p\ge 1} {\mathbb A}_p$.
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: Weights with bounded $A_p$ characteristic over all balls; $A_1$ via the maximal-function condition and $A_\infty=\cup_p A_p$.
nodes.label: def:1

nodes.name: Muckenhoupt's theorem
nodes.statement: We just recall that for $p\in(1,\infty)$, the maximal function ${\mathcal M}$ is bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ if and only if $\omega \in {\mathbb A}_p$.
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries
assumptions: $p\in(1,\infty)$
conclusions: the maximal function ${\mathcal M}$ is bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ if and only if $\omega \in {\mathbb A}_p$

nodes.name: Reverse Hölder class RH_p
nodes.statement: A weight $\omega \in RH_p$, $1<p<\infty$, if there is a constant $C$ such that for every ball $Q$, $$ \bigg( \aver{Q} \omega^p\,dx \bigg)^{1/p} \leq C \bigg(\aver{Q} \omega\,dx\bigg). $$ It is well known that ${\mathbb A}_\infty=\cup_{r>1} RH_r$. Thus, for $p=1$ it is understood that $RH_1={\mathbb A}_\infty$.
nodes.section: 1 Notations and preliminaries
nodes.label: def:2

nodes.name: Multi-frequency Hilbert transform
nodes.statement: In ${\mathbb R}$, consider an arbitrary collection of frequencies $\Theta:=(\xi_1,...,\xi_N)$ (assumed to be indexed by the increasing order $\xi_1< \xi_2< \cdots < \xi_N$). The associated multi-frequency Hilbert transform is the Fourier multiplier corresponding to the symbol $$ m(\xi) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -1, & \xi<\xi_1 \\ (-1)^{j+1}, & \xi_j<\xi<\xi_{j+1} \\ (-1)^{N+1}, & \xi>\xi_N. \end{array} \right. $$
nodes.section: The multi-frequency Hilbert transform
nodes.statement_short: Fourier multiplier with symbol alternating $\pm1$ on the intervals cut out by $\xi_1<\dots<\xi_N$.

nodes.name: Intervals associated to the frequencies
nodes.statement: Associated to $\Theta$, we have a collection of disjoint intervals $\Delta:=\{ (-\infty,\xi_1), (\xi_1,\xi_2),...,(\xi_N,\infty)\}$.
nodes.section: The multi-frequency Hilbert transform

nodes.name: Rubio de Francia's Littlewood-Paley inequality
nodes.statement: It is well-known by Rubio de Francia's work \cite{Rubio} that for $q\in(1,2]$, the functional \begin{equation} f \rightarrow \left( \sum_{\omega\in\Delta} \left|{\mathcal F}^{-1}[{\bf 1}_{\omega} {\mathcal F}f]\right|^q \right)^{\frac{1}{q}} \end{equation} is bounded on $L^p$ for $p\in(q',\infty)$.
nodes.section: The multi-frequency Hilbert transform
assumptions: for $q\in(1,2]$
conclusions: is bounded on $L^p$ for $p\in(q',\infty)$
nodes.statement_short: The $\ell^q$ square function over arbitrary intervals is $L^p$-bounded for $q\in(1,2]$, $p>q'$.

nodes.name: Rubio de Francia l^q functional (2)
nodes.statement: f \rightarrow \left( \sum_{\omega\in\Delta} \left|{\mathcal F}^{-1}[{\bf 1}_{\omega} {\mathcal F}f]\right|^q \right)^{\frac{1}{q}}
nodes.section: The multi-frequency Hilbert transform
nodes.label: eq:f

nodes.name: Uniformity in Rubio de Francia's result
nodes.statement: We point out that in Rubio de Francia's result, the obtained estimates do not depend on the collection of intervals $\Delta$. More precisely, excepted the end-point $p=q'$, the range $(q',\infty)$ is optimal for a uniform (with respect to the collection $\Delta$) $L^p$-boundedness of (\ref{eq:f}). So it is natural that for $q\to 1$ things are more difficult, which is illustrated by our multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund analysis.
nodes.section: The multi-frequency Hilbert transform
nodes.statement_short: Rubio de Francia's bounds are uniform in $\Delta$ with optimal range $(q',\infty)$, so the case $q\to1$ is harder.

nodes.name: Argument for the improved exponent when Theta=(1,...,N)
nodes.statement: Indeed, for example if one considers the particular case $\Theta:=(1,...,N)$, then following the notations of Remark \ref{rem:lem}, we have $\Theta^k =\{k,...,kN\}$ and so $\sharp \Theta^k = k(N-1)+1 \simeq k N$. Hence, in this situation we have observed (see Remark \ref{rem:lem}) that we can extend Lemma \ref{lem} to exponents $p\in[1,\infty]$ (the implicit constant appearing in (\ref{aze}) is only depending on $p$).
nodes.section: The multi-frequency Hilbert transform
nodes.statement_short: Direct count: for $\Theta=(1,\dots,N)$, $\sharp\Theta^k\simeq kN$, so Remark 1.2 extends Lemma 1.1 to all $p$.

nodes.name: Improved weighted exponent for Theta=(1,...,N)
nodes.statement: By this way, Theorem \ref{thm:weight} can be improved and we obtain a better exponent $$ \gamma=\frac{tp}{s^2}+\left|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}\right|.$$
nodes.section: The multi-frequency Hilbert transform
conclusions: $$ \gamma=\frac{tp}{s^2}+\left|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}\right|.$$
nodes.statement_short: For $\Theta=(1,\dots,N)$ Theorem 0.2 holds with the better exponent $tp/s^2+|1/2-1/s|$.

nodes.name: Convolution operators from disjoint frequency cubes
nodes.statement: Let $(Q_j)_{j=1,...,N}$ be a family of disjoint cubes and $\phi_j$ a smooth function with $\widehat{\phi_j}$ supported and adapted to $Q_j$. Then consider the linear operator given by $$ T(f) = \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_j \ast f.$$
nodes.section: Multi-frequency operators coming from a covering of the frequency space
nodes.statement_short: $T f=\sum_j \phi_j * f$ with $\widehat{\phi_j}$ adapted to disjoint cubes $Q_j$.

nodes.name: Covering operators are multi-frequency CZ operators
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that $T$ is a multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator, associated to the collection $\Theta:=(\xi_1,...,\xi_N)$ where for every $j$, $\xi_j:=c(Q_j)$ is the center of the ball $Q_j$. With $r_j$ the radius of $Q_j$, we have the regularity estimate $$ \sum_{j=1}^N \left|\nabla_{(x,y)}\ e^{i\xi_j\cdot(x-y)} \phi_j(x-y)\right| \lesssim |x-y|^{-n-1} \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{(r_j |x-y|)^{n+1}}{(1+r_j|x-y|)^{M}},$$ for every integer $M>0$.
nodes.section: Multi-frequency operators coming from a covering of the frequency space
conclusions: $T$ is a multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator, associated to the collection $\Theta:=(\xi_1,...,\xi_N)$ where for every $j$, $\xi_j:=c(Q_j)$ is the center of the ball $Q_j$.
assumptions: With $r_j$ the radius of $Q_j$
nodes.statement_short: $T=\sum_j\phi_j*f$ is multi-frequency CZ for the cube centers, with an explicit kernel regularity estimate.

nodes.name: L^p inequality for sums of frequency-localized convolutions
nodes.statement: So boundedness of $T$ (Theorem \ref{thm:boundedness}) yields the inequality \begin{equation} \left\| \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_j \ast f \right\|_{L^p} \lesssim C(r_1,...,r_N) N^{\left|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}\right|} \|f\|_{L^p}, \end{equation} with $$ C(r_1,...,r_N):= \sup_{t>0} \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{(r_j t)^{n+1}}{(1+r_jt)^{M}}.$$
nodes.section: Multi-frequency operators coming from a covering of the frequency space
conclusions: \left\| \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_j \ast f \right\|_{L^p} \lesssim C(r_1,...,r_N) N^{\left|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}\right|} \|f\|_{L^p},
nodes.statement_short: $\|\sum_j\phi_j*f\|_p\lesssim C(r_1,\dots,r_N)N^{|1/p-1/2|}\|f\|_p$ by Theorem 0.1.

nodes.name: Inequality (3)
nodes.statement: \left\| \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_j \ast f \right\|_{L^p} \lesssim C(r_1,...,r_N) N^{\left|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}\right|} \|f\|_{L^p},

nodes.name: Equal side-length cubes
nodes.statement: If the cubes $(Q_j)_j$ have an equal side-length, then as for Proposition \ref{prop}, simple arguments imply (\ref{eq:ex}) for $p\in[1,\infty]$ without the constant $C(r_1,...,r_N)$.

nodes.name: Dyadic collection of cubes
nodes.statement: If the collection $(Q_j)_j$ is dyadic: it exists a point $\xi_0$, $d(Q_j,\xi_0) \simeq r_{Q_j} \simeq 2^j$ then Littlewood-Paley theory implies (\ref{eq:ex}) without the factor $N^{|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}|}$ (in this case $C(r_1,...,r_N)\simeq 1$).

assumptions: If the collection $(Q_j)_j$ is dyadic: it exists a point $\xi_0$, $d(Q_j,\xi_0) \simeq r_{Q_j} \simeq 2^j$

nodes.name: Cubes with dyadic scales only
nodes.statement: If the cubes $(Q_j)$ have only the dyadic scale: $r_{Q_j} \simeq 2^j$ (but no assumptions on the centers of the balls) then Littlewood-Paley theory cannot be used. However, our previous results can be applied in this situation and so (\ref{eq:ex}) holds and $C(r_1,...,r_N) \simeq 1$.

assumptions: If the cubes $(Q_j)$ have only the dyadic scale: $r_{Q_j} \simeq 2^j$ (but no assumptions on the centers of the balls)

nodes.name: Maximally modulated Calderón-Zygmund inequalities
nodes.statement: For example, in \cite{GMS} Grafakos, Martell and Soria have studied maximal inequalities of the form $$ \left\| \sup_{j=1,...,N} \left| T( e^{i\theta_j\cdot} f) \right| \right\|_{L^p} \lesssim \|f\|_{L^p}$$ where $(\theta_j)_{j=1,...,N}$ is a collection of frequencies and $T$ a fixed Calder\'on-Zygmund operator.

nodes.statement_short: $L^p$ bounds for $\sup_j|T(e^{i\theta_j\cdot}f)|$ with $T$ a fixed CZ operator.

nodes.name: Variation-norm modulated Calderón-Zygmund inequalities
nodes.statement: We can ask the same question, for a variation norm variant: for $q\in[1,\infty)$ consider $$ \left(\sum_{j=1}^N \left| T( e^{i\theta_j\cdot} f) \right|^q \right)^{\frac{1}{q}}$$ and study its boundedness on $L^p$, with a sharp control of the behaviour with respect to $N$.
nodes.section: Multi-frequency operators coming from variation norm estimates
nodes.statement_short: Sharp-in-$N$ $L^p$ bounds for the $\ell^q$ functional $(\sum_j|T(e^{i\theta_j\cdot}f)|^q)^{1/q}$.

nodes.name: Linearization of the variation-norm functional
nodes.statement: By a linearization argument (involving Rademacher's functions), this $\ell^q$-functional can be realized as an average of modulated Calder\'on-Zygmund operators, associated to the collection $\Theta:=(\theta_j)_j$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 0.1 (outline)
nodes.statement: In this section, we aim to prove the weak $L^1$-estimate for a multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator, then Theorem \ref{thm:boundedness} will easily follow from interpolation and duality.

nodes.name: Weak (1,1) bound for multi-frequency CZ operators
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta=(\xi_1,...,\xi_N)$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies as above and $T$ be a Calder\'on-Zygmund operator relatively to $\Theta$. Then $T$ is of weak type $(1,1)$ with (uniformly with respect to $N$) $$ \|T\|_{L^1\to L^{1,\infty}} \lesssim N^{\frac{1}{2}}.$$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement: Consider $f$ a function in $L^1$ and $\lambda>0$, we use the Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition\footnote{In \cite{NOT}, the multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition is only described in ${\mathbb R}$. The proof is a combination of Lemma \ref{lem} and the usual Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition. Since both of them can be extended in a multi-dimensional framework, the multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition performed in \cite{NOT} still holds in ${\mathbb R}^n$.} of \cite{NOT} related to the collection of frequencies $\Theta$. So the function $f$ can be decomposed $f = g + \sum_{J\in {\bf J}} b_J$ with the following properties: \begin{itemize} \item ${\bf J}$ is a collection of balls and $(3J)_{J\in{\bf J}}$ has a bounded overlap; \item for each $J\in{\bf J}$, $b_J$ is supported in $3J$; \item we have \begin{equation} \sum_{J \in{\bf J}} |J| \lesssim \sqrt{N} \|f\|_{L^1} \lambda^{-1}; \end{equation} \item the ``good part'' $g$ satisfies \begin{equation} \|g\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \|f\|_{L^1} \sqrt{N} \lambda; \end{equation} \item the cubes $J$ satisfy \begin{equation} \|f\|_{L^1(J)} \lesssim |J|\lambda N^{-\frac{1}{2}} , \quad \|f-b_J\|_{L^2(J)} \lesssim \sqrt{|J|} \lambda; \end{equation} \item we have cancellation for all the frequencies of $\Theta$: for all $j=1,...,N$ and $J\in{\bf J}$, $\widehat{b_J}(\xi_j)=0$. \end{itemize} We aim to estimate the measure of the level-set $$ \Upsilon_\lambda:=\left\{x, |T(f)(x)|>\lambda\right\}.$$ With $b=\sum_J b_J$, we have \begin{align*} |\Upsilon_\lambda| & \leq \left|\left\{x, |T(g)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right| + \left|\left\{x, |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right| \\ & \lesssim \lambda^{-2} \|T(g)\|_{L^2}^2 + \left|\left\{x, |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right| \\ & \lesssim \lambda^{-1}\sqrt{N}\|f\|_{L^1} + \left|\left\{x, |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right|, \end{align*} where we used the $L^2$-boundedness of $T$. So it remains us to study the last term. Since (\ref{eq:sumJ}), we get $$ \left| \bigcup_{J\in {\bf J}} 4J \right| \lesssim \sum_{J} |J| \lesssim \sqrt{N} \|f\|_{L^1} \lambda^{-1}.$$ Consequently, it only remains to estimate the measure of the set $$ O_\lambda:= \left\{x \in \left(\bigcup_{J\in {\bf J}} 4J\right)^{c}, \quad |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}.$$ Since \begin{equation} |O_\lambda| \lesssim \lambda^{-1} \sum_{J} \|T(b_J)\|_{L^1((2J)^c)}, \end{equation} it is sufficient to estimate the $L^1$-norms. Consider $K$ the kernel of $T$ and a point $x_0\in \left(\bigcup_{J\in {\bf J}} 4J\right)^{c}$. Then, we can use the integral representation and we have $$ T(b)(x_0) = \int K(x_0,y) b(y) dy = \sum_{J} \int_{3J} K(x_0,y) b_J(y) dy.$$ To each $J$, we aim to take advantage of the cancellation properties of $b_J$, so we subtract the projection of $\left[y\to K(x_0,y)\right]$ on the space, spanned by $(e^{iy\cdot\eta})_{\eta\in \Theta}$. So we have \begin{align*} T(b)(x_0) & = \sum_{J}\sum_{j=1}^N \int_{3J} \left[K_j(x_0,y) - e^{i\xi_j \cdot c(J)} K_j(x_0,c(J))e^{-i\xi_j \cdot y}\right] b_J(y) dy \\ & = \sum_{J}\sum_{j=1}^N \int_{3J} \left[\widetilde{K}_{j}(x_0,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(x_0,c(J))\right]e^{i\xi_j\cdot (x_0-y)} b_J(y) dy \end{align*} where $c(J)$ is the center of $J$ and $\widetilde{K}_j(x,y):=K_j(x,y)e^{-i\xi_j \cdot (x-y)}$. We then write $$ T_j(b)(x_0) := \int \left[\widetilde{K}_{j}(x_0,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(x_0,c(J))\right]e^{i\xi_j \cdot (x_0-y)} b(y) dy.$$ such that $T(b) =\sum_j T_j(b)$. Due to the regularity assumption on $K$ (and so on $\widetilde{K}_j$), it comes for $y\in J$ and $x_0\in (2J)^c$ \begin{equation} \sum_{j=1}^N \left|\widetilde{K}_{j}(x_0,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(x_0,c(J))\right| \lesssim \frac{r_J}{|x_0-y|^{n+1}}. \end{equation} So we have $$ \|T(b_J)\|_{L^1((2J)^c)} \lesssim \iint_{|x-y|\geq r_J} \frac{r_J}{|x-y|^{n+1}} |b_J(y)| dxdy \lesssim \|b_J\|_{L^1} \lesssim |J| \lambda.$$ Finally, we obtain with (\ref{eq:Olambda}) that $$ |O_\lambda| \lesssim \sum_{J} |J| \lesssim \sqrt{N} \|f\|_{L^1} \lambda^{-1}, $$ which concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Optimality of the N^{1/2} bound
nodes.statement: Following \cite{NOT}, the bound of order $N^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is optimal for the multi-frequency decomposition and for the weak-$L^1$ estimate.
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Multi-frequency maximal sharp function
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies and $s\in[1,\infty)$. Consider a ball $Q$, we denote by ${\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}$ the projection operator (in the $L^s$-sense) on the subspace of $L^s(3Q)$, spanned by $(\exp {i\xi\cdot})_{\xi\in \Theta}$. Let us specify this projection operator: consider $E$ the finite dimensional sub-space of $L^s(3Q)$, spanned by $(e^{i\xi\cdot})_{\xi\in \Theta}$ and equipped with the $L^s(3Q)$-norm. Since $E$ is of finite dimension, then for every $f\in L^s(Q)$ there exists $v:={\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f)\in E$ such that $$ \|f-v\|_{L^s(3Q)} = \inf_{\phi\in E} \|f-\phi\|_{L^s(3Q)}.$$ This projection operator may depend on $s$, which is not important for our purpose so this is implicit in the notation and we forget it. \medskip\noindent Since $0\in E$, we obviously have \begin{equation} \|{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f)\|_{L^s(3Q)} \leq 2\|f\|_{L^s(Q)}. \end{equation} Then, we may define the maximal sharp function $$ {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (f)(x_0) := \sup_{x_0\in Q} \left(\aver{Q} \left|f-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f{\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}.$$
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators
nodes.statement_short: Sup over balls of the $L^s$ average of $f$ minus its best $L^s(3Q)$ approximation by exponentials with frequencies in $\Theta$.
nodes.label: def:max

nodes.name: Projection bound (9)
nodes.statement: \|{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f)\|_{L^s(3Q)} \leq 2\|f\|_{L^s(Q)}.

nodes.name: Classical sharp maximal function
nodes.statement: Note that the usual sharp maximal function is the one obtained for $\Theta:=\{0\}$ and in this situation it is well-known that the maximal sharp function satisfies a so-called Fefferman-Stein inequality (see \cite{FS}).
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Multi-frequency Fefferman-Stein inequality
nodes.statement: Let $s\in(1,\infty)$, $t\in[1,\infty)$ and $p \in(s,\infty)$ be fixed. Then for every function $f\in L^s$ and every weight $\omega\in RH_{t'}$, we have for every $p\geq s$ $$ \|f\|_{L^p(\omega)} \lesssim N^{\frac{tp}{s}\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left\| {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp(f) \right\|_{L^p(\omega)}.$$

assumptions: Let $s\in(1,\infty)$, $t\in[1,\infty)$ and $p \in(s,\infty)$ be fixed.
for every function $f\in L^s$ and every weight $\omega\in RH_{t'}$
conclusions: $$ \|f\|_{L^p(\omega)} \lesssim N^{\frac{tp}{s}\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left\| {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp(f) \right\|_{L^p(\omega)}.$$

nodes.label: prop:FeffermanStein

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: We make use on the abstract theory developed in \cite{AM} by Auscher and Martell. We also follow notations of \cite[Theorem 3.1]{AM}. Indeed, for each ball $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ we have the following $$ F(x) := |f(x)|^s \lesssim \left|f(x)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f{\bf 1}_Q)(x) \right|^s + \left|{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f{\bf 1}_Q)(x) \right|^s := G_Q(x)+H_Q(x). $$ By definition, it comes $$ \aver{Q} G_Q dx \leq \inf _{Q} {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (f)^s$$ and following Lemma \ref{lem} (with (\ref{eq:projection})) \begin{align*} \sup_{x\in Q} H_Q & = \|{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f {\bf 1}_Q)\|_{L^\infty(Q)}^s \lesssim N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left( \aver{3Q} |{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f {\bf 1}_Q)|^s dx\right) \\ & \lesssim N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left( \aver{Q} |f|^s dx\right) \lesssim N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \inf_Q {\mathcal M} F. \end{align*} So we can apply \cite[Theorem 3.1]{AM} (with $q=\infty$ and $a\simeq N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}}$) and by checking the behaviour of the constants with respect to ``$a$" in its proof, we obtain for every $p\geq 1$ $$ \left\| {\mathcal M}_s(f)^s \right\|_{L^p(\omega)} \lesssim N^{spt \max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left\| {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (f)^s \right\|_{L^p(\omega)},$$ which yields the desired result.

nodes.statement_short: Good-lambda inequality via the Auscher-Martell abstract theorem, with the $H_Q$ term controlled by Lemma 1.1.

nodes.name: Pointwise sharp-function bound for multi-frequency CZ operators
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be a Calder\'on-Zygmund operator relatively to $\Theta$ and $s\in(1,\infty)$. Then, we have the following pointwise estimate: $$ {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (T(f)) \lesssim N^{|\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{2}|} {\mathcal M}_s(f) .$$
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators
assumptions: Let $T$ be a Calder\'on-Zygmund operator relatively to $\Theta$ and $s\in(1,\infty)$.
conclusions: $$ {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (T(f)) \lesssim N^{|\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{2}|} {\mathcal M}_s(f) .$$
nodes.statement_short: $M^\sharp_{s,\Theta}(Tf)\lesssim N^{|1/s-1/2|}M_s f$ pointwise.
nodes.label: prop:maximal

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement: We follow the well-known proof for usual Calder\'on-Zygmund operators and adapt the arguments to the current situation. So consider a point $x_0$ and a ball $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $x_0$, we have to estimate $$ \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}.$$ We split the function into a local part $f_0$ and an off-diagonal part $f_\infty$: $$f=f_0+f_\infty:= f{\bf 1}_{10 Q} + f {\bf 1}_{(10 Q)^c}.$$ By definition of the projection operator, we know that \begin{align*} \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} & \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} \\ & \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_0) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} + \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}. \end{align*} For the local part, we use boundedness in $L^s$ of the operator $T$ (Proposition \ref{prop:bound}), hence \begin{align*} \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_0)\right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} & \lesssim |Q|^{-\frac{1}{s}} \|T(f_0)\|_{L^s(Q)} \lesssim N^{(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s})} \left(|Q|^{-\frac{1}{s}} \|f_0\|_{L^s}\right) \\ & \lesssim N^{|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}|} {\mathcal M}_s(f)(x_0). \end{align*} Then let us focus on the second part, involving $f_\infty$. \\ We use the decomposition (with an integral representation) since we are in the off-diagonal case: for $x\in Q$ $$ T(f_\infty)(x) = \sum_{j=1}^N \int K_j(x,y) f_\infty(y) dy.$$ Consider the following function, defined on $3Q$ by (where $c(Q)$ is the center of $Q$) $$ \Phi:= x\in 3Q \rightarrow \sum_{j=1}^N \int e^{i\xi_j\cdot (x-c(Q))} K_j(c(Q),y) f_\infty(y) dy.$$ So $\Phi \in E$ (see Definition \ref{def:max}) and hence \begin{equation} \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-\Phi \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}. \end{equation} If we set $\widetilde{K}_j(x,z):=K_j(x,z)e^{-i\xi_j\cdot (x-z)}$, then $$ T(f_\infty)(x) -\Phi(x) = \sum_j \int \left[\widetilde{K}_{j}(x,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(c(Q),y)\right] e^{i\xi_j(x-y)} f_\infty(y) dy.$$ From the regularity assumption on the kernels $K_j$'s, we have for $y\in (10 Q)^c$ \begin{equation} \sum_{j} \left| \widetilde{K}_{j}(x,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(c(Q),y) \right| \lesssim r_Q \sup_{z\in Q} \sum_j \left| \nabla_{x} \widetilde{K}_{j}(z,y)\right| \lesssim r_Q^{-n}\left(1+\frac{d(y,Q)}{r_Q}\right)^{-n-1}. \end{equation} We also have (since $y\in (10 Q)^c$ and $x,c(Q)\in Q$) \begin{align*} \left| T(f_\infty)(x) -\Phi(x)\right| & \lesssim \int_{|z|\geq 10 r_Q} r_Q^{-n}\left(1+\frac{|x-c(Q)-z|}{r_Q}\right)^{-n-1} |f(c(Q)+z)| dz \\ & \lesssim \int_{|z|\geq 5 r_Q} r_Q^{-n}\left(1+\frac{|z|}{r_Q}\right)^{-n-1} |f(x_0+z)| dz \\ & \lesssim {\mathcal M}(f)(x_0), \end{align*} which concludes the proof.

nodes.statement_short: Local/off-diagonal splitting as in the classical CZ argument. The far part is compared with an exponential sum $\Phi\in E$ built from the kernels at $c(Q)$.

nodes.statement: \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-\Phi \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}.

nodes.name: Weighted bounds for s >= 2
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies. For $p\in (2,\infty)$, $s\in[2,p)$ and $t\in(1,\infty)$, a multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator $T$ is bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ for every weight $\omega \in RH_{t'} \cap {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$ with $$ \|T\|_{L^p(\omega) \to L^p(\omega)} \lesssim N^{\frac{tp}{2s}+\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}\right)}.$$

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.3
nodes.statement: Using Propositions \ref{prop:FeffermanStein} and \ref{prop:maximal}, it follows that for $p>s\geq 2$ (assuming $\omega \in {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$) \begin{align*} \|T(f) \|_{L^p(\omega)} & \lesssim N^{\frac{tp}{2s}} \left\| {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp [T(f)] \right\|_{L^p(\omega)} \\ & \lesssim N^{\frac{tp}{2s}+\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}\right)} \left\| {\mathcal M}_s(f) \right\|_{L^p(\omega)} \\ & \lesssim N^{\frac{tp}{2s}+\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}\right)} \left\| f \right\|_{L^p(\omega)}, \end{align*} where we used weighted boundedness of the maximal function since $\omega \in {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$.

nodes.name: Domain Omega and boundary Gamma
nodes.statement: Consider also $\Omega$ a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that its boundary $\Gamma:=\overline{\Omega}\setminus \Omega$ is an hyper-manifold of Hausdorff dimension $n-1$.

nodes.name: Generalized Bochner-Riesz multiplier
nodes.statement: For $\delta>0$, we then define the generalized Bochner-Riesz multiplier, given by $$ R_{\Omega,\delta}(f) (x) := \int_\Omega e^{ix\cdot \xi} \widehat{f}(\xi) m_\delta d\xi,$$ where $m_\delta$ is a smooth symbol supported in $\overline{\Omega}$ and satisfying in $\Omega$ $$ | \partial^\alpha m_\delta(\xi)| \lesssim d(\xi,\Gamma)^{\delta-|\alpha|}.$$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.statement_short: $R_{\Omega,\delta}$: multiplier with symbol supported in $\overline\Omega$ vanishing like $d(\xi,\Gamma)^\delta$ at the boundary.

nodes.name: Whitney covering
nodes.statement: We first use a Whitney covering $(O_i)_i$ of $\Omega$. That is a collection of sub-balls such that \begin{itemize} \item the collection $(O_i)_i$ covers $\Omega$ and has a bounded overlap; \item the radius $r_{O_i}$ is equivalent to $d(O_i,\Gamma)$.
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
differentia: the collection $(O_i)_i$ covers $\Omega$ and has a bounded overlap;

nodes.name: Adapted partition of unity
nodes.statement: Associated to this collection, we build a partition of the unity $(\chi_i)_i$ of smooth functions such that $\chi_i$ is supported on $O_i$ with $$ \sum_i \chi_i(\xi) = {\bf 1}_{\Omega}(\xi)$$ and $\|\partial^\alpha \chi_i\|_\infty \lesssim r_{O_i}^{-|\alpha|}$.
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition of the Bochner-Riesz multiplier
nodes.statement: Then, $R_{\delta}$ may be written as $$ R_{\delta}(f) (x) = \sum_{j=-\infty}^\infty T_j(f)(x),$$ with \begin{align} T_j(f)(x) & :=\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{l,}{2^j \leq r_{O_l}< 2^{j+1}}} \int_\Omega e^{ix\cdot \xi} \widehat{f}(\xi) m_\delta(\xi) \chi_l(\xi) d\xi \nonumber \\ & =2^{j\delta} U_j(f)(x), \end{align} where we set $$ U_j(f)(x):= \sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{l,}{2^j \leq r_{O_l}< 2^{j+1}}} \int_\Omega e^{ix\cdot \xi} \widehat{f}(\xi) (2^{-j\delta} m_\delta(\xi)) \chi_l(\xi) d\xi.$$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.statement_short: Split $R_\delta=\sum_j T_j=\sum_j 2^{j\delta}U_j$ by grouping Whitney balls of radius $\sim2^j$.

nodes.name: Decomposition T_j = 2^{j delta} U_j (12)
nodes.statement: T_j(f)(x) & :=\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{l,}{2^j \leq r_{O_l}< 2^{j+1}}} \int_\Omega e^{ix\cdot \xi} \widehat{f}(\xi) m_\delta(\xi) \chi_l(\xi) d\xi \nonumber \\ & =2^{j\delta} U_j(f)(x),
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.label: eq:dec

nodes.name: U_j is a multi-frequency CZ operator
nodes.statement: {\bf Observation :} The main idea is to observe that the operator $U_j$ is a multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator associated to the collection $$ \Theta_j :=\{ c(O_l), \ 2^j \leq r_{O_l}< 2^{j+1} \} \qquad \textrm{with} \qquad \sharp \Theta_j \simeq 2^{-j(n-1)}.$$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
conclusions: the operator $U_j$ is a multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator associated to the collection
nodes.statement_short: Each $U_j$ is a multi-frequency CZ operator for the centers of the radius-$2^j$ Whitney balls, about $2^{-j(n-1)}$ frequencies.

nodes.name: Easy bounds for U_j
nodes.statement: Uniformly with $j\lesssim 0$, the multiplier $U_j$ is a convolution operation with a kernel $K_j$ satisfying $$ \|K_j\|_{L^1} \lesssim 2^{-j \frac{n-1}{2}}.$$ Hence, it follows that $U_j$ is bounded on Lebesgue space $L^p$ for every $p\in[1,\infty]$. Moreover for every $s\in[1,2]$, $p\in(s,\infty)$ and every weight $\omega\in {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$, $U_j$ is bounded on $L^p(\omega)$ with $$ \| U_j\|_{L^p(\omega) \rightarrow L^p(\omega)} \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{s}}.$$

for every $s\in[1,2]$, $p\in(s,\infty)$ and every weight $\omega\in {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$

nodes.label: prop

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.1
nodes.statement: The operator $U_j$ is a Fourier multiplier, associated to the symbol $$\sigma_j(\xi):=\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{l,}{2^j \leq r_{O_l}< 2^{j+1}}} (2^{-j\delta} m_\delta(\xi)) \chi_l(\xi).$$ Since the considered balls $(O_l)_l$ are almost disjoint, it comes that $$ \|\sigma_j\|_{L^2} \lesssim |\{\xi, d(\xi,\partial \Omega)\simeq 2^j \}|^{\frac{1}{2}} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{2}}.$$ Moreover, using regularity assumptions on $m_\delta$, we deduce that for every $\alpha$ $$ \|\partial^\alpha \sigma_j\|_{L^2} \lesssim 2^{-j|\alpha|} |\{\xi, d(\xi,\partial \Omega) \simeq 2^j \}|^{\frac{1}{2}} \lesssim 2^{j(\frac{1}{2}-|\alpha|)}.$$ So with $K_j:= \mathcal{F}(\sigma_j)$, it follows that for any integer $M$ \begin{equation} \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^2} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{2}}. \end{equation} Hence $$ \left\| K_j\right\|_{L^1} \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{2}}.$$ Using Minkowski inequality, we deduce that for every $p\in[1,\infty]$ $$ \| U_j\|_{L^p \to L^p} \lesssim \|K_j\|_{L^1} \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{2}}.$$ Let us now focus on the second claim about weighted estimates. Using integrations by parts for computing the kernel $K_j$, it comes for any integer $M$ \begin{equation} \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim 2^{j}. \end{equation} By interpolation with (\ref{eq:L^2}), for $s\in[1,2]$ we get \begin{equation} \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^{s'}} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{s}}, \end{equation} which gives $$ U_j(f) \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{s}} {\mathcal M}_{s}(f).$$ Hence, for every $p> s$ and every weight $\omega \in {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$ $$ \|U_j\|_{L^p(\omega) \to L^p(\omega)} \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{s}}.$$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.statement_short: Weighted $L^2$ bounds on the symbol and its derivatives give kernel decay. Interpolating $L^2$ and $L^\infty$ kernel bounds gives $U_j f\lesssim2^{-j(n-1)/s}M_s f$.

nodes.name: Weighted L^2 kernel bound (13)
nodes.statement: \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^2} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{2}}.
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.label: eq:L^2

nodes.name: Weighted L^infty kernel bound (14)
nodes.statement: \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim 2^{j}.
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Weighted L^{s'} kernel bound (15)
nodes.statement: \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^{s'}} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{s}},

nodes.name: Comparison of the easy bounds with Corollary 3.3
nodes.statement: In this context, $\sharp \Theta_j \simeq 2^{-j(n-1)}$, so the constant $2^{-j \frac{n-1}{s}}$ is equivalent to $(\sharp \Theta_j)^{\frac{1}{s}}$ and this is a better constant than the one obtained in Corollary \ref{cor} (for a subclass of ${\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$ weights). \\ So improving these ``easy bounds'' means to obtain inequalities such as $$ \| U_j\|_{L^p(\omega) \rightarrow L^p(\omega)} \lesssim (\sharp \Theta_j)^{\gamma}$$ for some better exponent $\gamma<\frac{1}{s}$.
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.statement_short: The easy bound is $(\sharp\Theta_j)^{1/s}$, better than Corollary 3.3; progress means an exponent $\gamma<1/s$.

nodes.name: Improving the exponent gamma for Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.statement: {\bf Question :} The general approach, developed in the previous section, only allows to get an exponent $$ \gamma=\frac{tp}{2s}+\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}\right)$$ (with some $s\in[2,p)$) which is bigger than $\frac{1}{2}$ (since $p>s\geq 2$ and $t>1$). So to improve this exponent $\gamma$, two things seem to be crucial: \begin{itemize} \item to extend the use of Lemma \ref{lem} for $p\geq 2$ which would allow us to get an exponent $\frac{tp}{s^2}$ instead of $\frac{tp}{2s}$; \item to use the geometry of the boundary $\Gamma$ to get better exponents, even for the unweighted estimates. Indeed, for example for the unit ball (using its non vanishing curvature), we know that (see \cite{Lee, survey}) $$ \|U_j\|_{L^p\to L^p} \lesssim 2^{-j\delta(p)}$$ with if $n=2$ $$ \delta(p):= \max\left\{ 2\left|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{p}\right|-\frac{1}{2},0 \right\}.$$ and if $n\geq 3$ and $p\geq \frac{2(n+2)}{n}$ or $p\leq \frac{2(n+2)}{n+4}$ $$ \delta(p):= \max\left\{ n\left|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{p}\right|-\frac{1}{2},0 \right\}.$$ \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
nodes.statement_short: How to lower the exponent $\gamma$ below $1/2$: extend Lemma 1.1 to $p\ge2$ and exploit the geometry of $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Bochner-Riesz bounds for the unit ball
nodes.statement: Indeed, for example for the unit ball (using its non vanishing curvature), we know that (see \cite{Lee, survey}) $$ \|U_j\|_{L^p\to L^p} \lesssim 2^{-j\delta(p)}$$ with if $n=2$ $$ \delta(p):= \max\left\{ 2\left|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{p}\right|-\frac{1}{2},0 \right\}.$$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers
assumptions: for the unit ball (using its non vanishing curvature)
conclusions: $$ \|U_j\|_{L^p\to L^p} \lesssim 2^{-j\delta(p)}$$
nodes.statement_short: For the unit ball, $\|U_j\|_{p\to p}\lesssim2^{-j\delta(p)}$ with explicit $\delta(p)$ in $n=2$ and in $n\ge3$ outside a range of $p$.

nodes.name: Multi-frequency CZ decomposition
nodes.statement: Consider $f$ a function in $L^1$ and $\lambda>0$, we use the Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition\footnote{In \cite{NOT}, the multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition is only described in ${\mathbb R}$. The proof is a combination of Lemma \ref{lem} and the usual Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition. Since both of them can be extended in a multi-dimensional framework, the multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition performed in \cite{NOT} still holds in ${\mathbb R}^n$.} of \cite{NOT} related to the collection of frequencies $\Theta$. So the function $f$ can be decomposed $f = g + \sum_{J\in {\bf J}} b_J$ with the following properties:
nodes.statement_short: Apply the multi-frequency Calderón-Zygmund decomposition of [NOT]
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Bounded overlap of the balls
nodes.statement: ${\bf J}$ is a collection of balls and $(3J)_{J\in{\bf J}}$ has a bounded overlap;
nodes.statement_short: Property of the decomposition: bounded overlap of the balls
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Support of the bad parts
nodes.statement: for each $J\in{\bf J}$, $b_J$ is supported in $3J$;
nodes.statement_short: Property of the decomposition: support of the bad parts
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Total measure of the balls
nodes.statement: we have \begin{equation} \sum_{J \in{\bf J}} |J| \lesssim \sqrt{N} \|f\|_{L^1} \lambda^{-1}; \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Property of the decomposition: total measure of the balls
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: L^2 bound on the good part
nodes.statement: the ``good part'' $g$ satisfies \begin{equation} \|g\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \|f\|_{L^1} \sqrt{N} \lambda; \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Property of the decomposition: l^2 bound on the good part
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Bounds on f and b_J on the balls
nodes.statement: the cubes $J$ satisfy \begin{equation} \|f\|_{L^1(J)} \lesssim |J|\lambda N^{-\frac{1}{2}} , \quad \|f-b_J\|_{L^2(J)} \lesssim \sqrt{|J|} \lambda; \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Property of the decomposition: bounds on f and b_j on the balls
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Cancellation at the frequencies
nodes.statement: we have cancellation for all the frequencies of $\Theta$: for all $j=1,...,N$ and $J\in{\bf J}$, $\widehat{b_J}(\xi_j)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Property of the decomposition: cancellation at the frequencies
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Level set
nodes.statement: We aim to estimate the measure of the level-set $$ \Upsilon_\lambda:=\left\{x, |T(f)(x)|>\lambda\right\}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the level set $\Upsilon_\lambda$
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Good part estimate
nodes.statement: With $b=\sum_J b_J$, we have \begin{align*} |\Upsilon_\lambda| & \leq \left|\left\{x, |T(g)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right| + \left|\left\{x, |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right| \\ & \lesssim \lambda^{-2} \|T(g)\|_{L^2}^2 + \left|\left\{x, |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right| \\ & \lesssim \lambda^{-1}\sqrt{N}\|f\|_{L^1} + \left|\left\{x, |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}\right|, \end{align*} where we used the $L^2$-boundedness of $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Split into good and bad parts; bound the good part via $L^2$ boundedness and (5)
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Reduction to bad part
nodes.statement: So it remains us to study the last term.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the bad part
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Exceptional set
nodes.statement: Since (\ref{eq:sumJ}), we get $$ \left| \bigcup_{J\in {\bf J}} 4J \right| \lesssim \sum_{J} |J| \lesssim \sqrt{N} \|f\|_{L^1} \lambda^{-1}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the measure of the enlarged balls $\cup 4J$
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Reduction to O_lambda
nodes.statement: Consequently, it only remains to estimate the measure of the set $$ O_\lambda:= \left\{x \in \left(\bigcup_{J\in {\bf J}} 4J\right)^{c}, \quad |T(b)(x)|>\lambda/2\right\}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the set $O_\lambda$ off the enlarged balls
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Reduction to L^1 norms
nodes.statement: Since \begin{equation} |O_\lambda| \lesssim \lambda^{-1} \sum_{J} \|T(b_J)\|_{L^1((2J)^c)}, \end{equation} it is sufficient to estimate the $L^1$-norms.
nodes.statement_short: Chebyshev: suffices to bound $\|T b_J\|_{L^1((2J)^c)}$
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Kernel representation
nodes.statement: Consider $K$ the kernel of $T$ and a point $x_0\in \left(\bigcup_{J\in {\bf J}} 4J\right)^{c}$. Then, we can use the integral representation and we have $$ T(b)(x_0) = \int K(x_0,y) b(y) dy = \sum_{J} \int_{3J} K(x_0,y) b_J(y) dy.$$
nodes.statement_short: Write $T(b)(x_0)$ via the kernel representation
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Subtract projection
nodes.statement: To each $J$, we aim to take advantage of the cancellation properties of $b_J$, so we subtract the projection of $\left[y\to K(x_0,y)\right]$ on the space, spanned by $(e^{iy\cdot\eta})_{\eta\in \Theta}$. So we have \begin{align*} T(b)(x_0) & = \sum_{J}\sum_{j=1}^N \int_{3J} \left[K_j(x_0,y) - e^{i\xi_j \cdot c(J)} K_j(x_0,c(J))e^{-i\xi_j \cdot y}\right] b_J(y) dy \\ & = \sum_{J}\sum_{j=1}^N \int_{3J} \left[\widetilde{K}_{j}(x_0,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(x_0,c(J))\right]e^{i\xi_j\cdot (x_0-y)} b_J(y) dy \end{align*} where $c(J)$ is the center of $J$ and $\widetilde{K}_j(x,y):=K_j(x,y)e^{-i\xi_j \cdot (x-y)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the projection of the kernel onto the exponentials, using cancellation of $b_J$
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Define T_j(b)
nodes.statement: We then write $$ T_j(b)(x_0) := \int \left[\widetilde{K}_{j}(x_0,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(x_0,c(J))\right]e^{i\xi_j \cdot (x_0-y)} b(y) dy.$$ such that $T(b) =\sum_j T_j(b)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the pieces $T_j(b)$
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Kernel difference bound
nodes.statement: Due to the regularity assumption on $K$ (and so on $\widetilde{K}_j$), it comes for $y\in J$ and $x_0\in (2J)^c$ \begin{equation} \sum_{j=1}^N \left|\widetilde{K}_{j}(x_0,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(x_0,c(J))\right| \lesssim \frac{r_J}{|x_0-y|^{n+1}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Kernel regularity gives the difference bound (8)
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: L^1 estimate
nodes.statement: So we have $$ \|T(b_J)\|_{L^1((2J)^c)} \lesssim \iint_{|x-y|\geq r_J} \frac{r_J}{|x-y|^{n+1}} |b_J(y)| dxdy \lesssim \|b_J\|_{L^1} \lesssim |J| \lambda.$$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to get $\|T b_J\|_{L^1((2J)^c)}\lesssim|J|\lambda$
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Finally, we obtain with (\ref{eq:Olambda}) that $$ |O_\lambda| \lesssim \sum_{J} |J| \lesssim \sqrt{N} \|f\|_{L^1} \lambda^{-1}, $$ which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $J$ using (4) to conclude
nodes.section: 2 Unweighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Auscher-Martell framework
nodes.statement: We make use on the abstract theory developed in \cite{AM} by Auscher and Martell. We also follow notations of \cite[Theorem 3.1]{AM}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the Auscher-Martell good-lambda framework
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Split F=G_Q+H_Q
nodes.statement: Indeed, for each ball $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ we have the following $$ F(x) := |f(x)|^s \lesssim \left|f(x)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f{\bf 1}_Q)(x) \right|^s + \left|{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f{\bf 1}_Q)(x) \right|^s := G_Q(x)+H_Q(x). $$
nodes.statement_short: Split $|f|^s$ into oscillation $G_Q$ and projection $H_Q$
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Bounds on G_Q and H_Q
nodes.statement: By definition, it comes $$ \aver{Q} G_Q dx \leq \inf _{Q} {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (f)^s$$ and following Lemma \ref{lem} (with (\ref{eq:projection})) \begin{align*} \sup_{x\in Q} H_Q & = \|{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f {\bf 1}_Q)\|_{L^\infty(Q)}^s \lesssim N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left( \aver{3Q} |{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f {\bf 1}_Q)|^s dx\right) \\ & \lesssim N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left( \aver{Q} |f|^s dx\right) \lesssim N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \inf_Q {\mathcal M} F. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $G_Q$ by the sharp function and $H_Q$ by Lemma 1.1 and (9)
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Apply good-lambda theorem
nodes.statement: So we can apply \cite[Theorem 3.1]{AM} (with $q=\infty$ and $a\simeq N^{s\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}}$) and by checking the behaviour of the constants with respect to ``$a$" in its proof, we obtain for every $p\geq 1$ $$ \left\| {\mathcal M}_s(f)^s \right\|_{L^p(\omega)} \lesssim N^{spt \max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{s}\}} \left\| {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (f)^s \right\|_{L^p(\omega)},$$ which yields the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Auscher-Martell Theorem 3.1 tracking the constant $a$
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement: We follow the well-known proof for usual Calder\'on-Zygmund operators and adapt the arguments to the current situation.
nodes.statement_short: Follow the classical CZ sharp-function argument
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Fix ball
nodes.statement: So consider a point $x_0$ and a ball $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $x_0$, we have to estimate $$ \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Fix $x_0\in Q$ and the oscillation to estimate
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Local/off-diagonal split
nodes.statement: We split the function into a local part $f_0$ and an off-diagonal part $f_\infty$: $$f=f_0+f_\infty:= f{\bf 1}_{10 Q} + f {\bf 1}_{(10 Q)^c}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Split $f=f_0+f_\infty$
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Projection minimality
nodes.statement: By definition of the projection operator, we know that \begin{align*} \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} & \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} \\ & \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_0) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} + \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use minimality of the projection to separate the two parts
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Local part
nodes.statement: For the local part, we use boundedness in $L^s$ of the operator $T$ (Proposition \ref{prop:bound}), hence \begin{align*} \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_0)\right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} & \lesssim |Q|^{-\frac{1}{s}} \|T(f_0)\|_{L^s(Q)} \lesssim N^{(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s})} \left(|Q|^{-\frac{1}{s}} \|f_0\|_{L^s}\right) \\ & \lesssim N^{|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}|} {\mathcal M}_s(f)(x_0). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Local part via $L^s$ boundedness of $T$
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Off-diagonal representation
nodes.statement: Then let us focus on the second part, involving $f_\infty$. \\ We use the decomposition (with an integral representation) since we are in the off-diagonal case: for $x\in Q$ $$ T(f_\infty)(x) = \sum_{j=1}^N \int K_j(x,y) f_\infty(y) dy.$$
nodes.statement_short: Off-diagonal part via the integral representation
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Comparison function Phi
nodes.statement: Consider the following function, defined on $3Q$ by (where $c(Q)$ is the center of $Q$) $$ \Phi:= x\in 3Q \rightarrow \sum_{j=1}^N \int e^{i\xi_j\cdot (x-c(Q))} K_j(c(Q),y) f_\infty(y) dy.$$ So $\Phi \in E$ (see Definition \ref{def:max}) and hence \begin{equation} \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-\Phi \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\Phi\in E$ and compare with it (10)
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Rewrite difference
nodes.statement: If we set $\widetilde{K}_j(x,z):=K_j(x,z)e^{-i\xi_j\cdot (x-z)}$, then $$ T(f_\infty)(x) -\Phi(x) = \sum_j \int \left[\widetilde{K}_{j}(x,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(c(Q),y)\right] e^{i\xi_j(x-y)} f_\infty(y) dy.$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $T f_\infty-\Phi$ with modulated kernels
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Kernel estimate
nodes.statement: From the regularity assumption on the kernels $K_j$'s, we have for $y\in (10 Q)^c$ \begin{equation} \sum_{j} \left| \widetilde{K}_{j}(x,y) - \widetilde{K}_j(c(Q),y) \right| \lesssim r_Q \sup_{z\in Q} \sum_j \left| \nabla_{x} \widetilde{K}_{j}(z,y)\right| \lesssim r_Q^{-n}\left(1+\frac{d(y,Q)}{r_Q}\right)^{-n-1}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Kernel regularity estimate (11)
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: We also have (since $y\in (10 Q)^c$ and $x,c(Q)\in Q$) \begin{align*} \left| T(f_\infty)(x) -\Phi(x)\right| & \lesssim \int_{|z|\geq 10 r_Q} r_Q^{-n}\left(1+\frac{|x-c(Q)-z|}{r_Q}\right)^{-n-1} |f(c(Q)+z)| dz \\ & \lesssim \int_{|z|\geq 5 r_Q} r_Q^{-n}\left(1+\frac{|z|}{r_Q}\right)^{-n-1} |f(x_0+z)| dz \\ & \lesssim {\mathcal M}(f)(x_0), \end{align*} which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Bound by $Mf(x_0)$ and conclude
nodes.section: 3 Weighted estimates for multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operators

nodes.name: Symbol
nodes.statement: The operator $U_j$ is a Fourier multiplier, associated to the symbol $$\sigma_j(\xi):=\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{l,}{2^j \leq r_{O_l}< 2^{j+1}}} (2^{-j\delta} m_\delta(\xi)) \chi_l(\xi).$$
nodes.statement_short: Identify the symbol $\sigma_j$ of $U_j$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: L^2 bound on symbol
nodes.statement: Since the considered balls $(O_l)_l$ are almost disjoint, it comes that $$ \|\sigma_j\|_{L^2} \lesssim |\{\xi, d(\xi,\partial \Omega)\simeq 2^j \}|^{\frac{1}{2}} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{2}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: $L^2$ bound on $\sigma_j$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Derivative bounds
nodes.statement: Moreover, using regularity assumptions on $m_\delta$, we deduce that for every $\alpha$ $$ \|\partial^\alpha \sigma_j\|_{L^2} \lesssim 2^{-j|\alpha|} |\{\xi, d(\xi,\partial \Omega) \simeq 2^j \}|^{\frac{1}{2}} \lesssim 2^{j(\frac{1}{2}-|\alpha|)}.$$
nodes.statement_short: $L^2$ bounds on derivatives of $\sigma_j$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Kernel L^1 bound
nodes.statement: So with $K_j:= \mathcal{F}(\sigma_j)$, it follows that for any integer $M$ \begin{equation} \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^2} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{2}}. \end{equation} Hence $$ \left\| K_j\right\|_{L^1} \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{2}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Weighted $L^2$ kernel bound (13), hence $L^1$ bound on $K_j$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Unweighted bound
nodes.statement: Using Minkowski inequality, we deduce that for every $p\in[1,\infty]$ $$ \| U_j\|_{L^p \to L^p} \lesssim \|K_j\|_{L^1} \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{2}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Unweighted $L^p$ bound by Minkowski
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: L^infty kernel bound
nodes.statement: Let us now focus on the second claim about weighted estimates. Using integrations by parts for computing the kernel $K_j$, it comes for any integer $M$ \begin{equation} \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim 2^{j}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $L^\infty$ kernel bound (14) by integration by parts
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Interpolation
nodes.statement: By interpolation with (\ref{eq:L^2}), for $s\in[1,2]$ we get \begin{equation} \left\| (1+2^{j}|\cdot|)^{M} K_j\right\|_{L^{s'}} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{s}}, \end{equation} which gives $$ U_j(f) \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{s}} {\mathcal M}_{s}(f).$$
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate to an $L^{s'}$ bound and get domination by $M_s$
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Weighted conclusion
nodes.statement: Hence, for every $p> s$ and every weight $\omega \in {\mathbb A}_{\frac{p}{s}}$ $$ \|U_j\|_{L^p(\omega) \to L^p(\omega)} \lesssim 2^{-j\frac{n-1}{s}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Weighted bound from the $M_s$ domination
nodes.section: 4 Connexion to Bochner-Riesz multipliers

nodes.name: Lebesgue space notation
nodes.statement: We write $L^p$ for $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R})$ or $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n,{\mathbb C})$.
